title: Prince in court dress, stride B (tinted)
prompt:
Prince Bel-Azor walking to the right, exactly the figure, costume, colours, scale and head height of prince-court-tinted.webp (attach it, and prince-court-stride-a-tinted.webp if already drawn, which must match it in every detail but the legs and arms). A full stride with the RIGHT leg forward, heel down, and the left leg straight behind on its toes; the arms swing opposite to the legs. Both feet on one level ground line at the very bottom of the canvas; the head at the same height as in the standing pose. Nothing changes between the two frames but the legs and arms: same tights, belt, cloak, sword and shield. Render it like a frame of a hand stencil-coloured 1903 Méliès print, not an illustration: a soft-focus black-and-white photograph of a real stage performer in costume (silvery greys, deep blacks, gentle film grain and a little halation), with only a few flat, translucent aniline dye washes laid over by stencil (sea-green teal, orange-yellow, rose and coral red, pale sky blue, magenta), each bleeding slightly past its edges and a little out of register, and large areas left untinted grey; a simple theatre costume of cloth, tights, wig and painted card props with little fine detail and no gold filigree; flat frontal stage lighting; no ink outlines and no glossy finish. Isolated on a transparent background (or flat pure magenta #FF00FF if transparency is unavailable).
Image 1 is the standing character and fixes the exact costume, colours, face, belt, tights, cape, armour and prop sides. Do not reinterpret the costume. Preserve anatomically coherent hands gripping any carried weapons; exactly two arms and two legs. Draw a clearly separated full walking stride with the two feet apart, never the standing pose. Both soles meet the same horizontal baseline at the bottom; keep the standing head and plume/circlet height. No ground or cast shadow. Canvas aspect ratio 220:360; one isolated transparent sprite, target delivery 220 x 360. Court dress remains bareheaded and unarmoured with no sword or shield; copy the standing reference’s tights and belt colours exactly.
Image 2 is the already drawn stride A and is the edit target. Match its face and every garment, tights colour, belt colour and buckle, cape pattern, sword and shield exactly. Change only the limbs to the OPPOSITE stride: right leg forward on its heel, left leg behind on its toes, arms counter-swinging. Do not copy the leg arrangement from A. Keep its torso, head, costume details and head/foot heights unchanged. No costume redesign or additional props.
CRITICAL GAIT CORRECTION: the previous B image duplicated A and is rejected. In the new B, the image-nearest LEFT leg must be visibly stretched STRAIGHT BACK toward the LEFT side of the canvas, rear heel raised and toe touching the ground. The farther RIGHT leg must come FORWARD toward the RIGHT with a conspicuously BENT KNEE over the forward heel, calf more upright, heel down. This must have a DIFFERENT knee silhouette and thigh overlap from A, not two copies of the same legs. The near thigh runs backward from the hip; the far thigh comes forward from behind it. Keep the pelvis, torso and head at their original height. Both feet meet the bottom baseline. The arms must also move: the free near left arm swings FORWARD with its hand out at waist height, the far right arm swings BACK with its hand low behind the hip; no hand held frozen over his chest. Keep the identical tights, belt, face and every costume colour from A. Edit the gait, do not mirror the whole character.
